claim_verdicts.evidence: (round 1, unchanged) "It states that objects should have only one responsibility and that they should have only one reason to change." Also: "the single responsibility principle (SRP) applied to classes, which states that a class should only have one reason to change." (microservice-application-design.md:136)

(round 1, re-checked) git show stage-0:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Clean/PlaceOrderSplit.cs: line 6 `public static string Place(...)`; lines 18, 27, 33, 36 `private static` FirstProblemWith, TotalWithShippingVnd, Save, Notify; Save and Notify are expression-bodied Console.WriteLine. Code block lines 18-37 matches source character-for-character.

Line 30: `return totalVnd + (totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000);` inside TotalWithShippingVnd. Lines 20-23 are the input `if` checks in FirstProblemWith; a `lines.Count > 20` check is one more `if` there. Line 34 prints "saving order for customer ...", line 37 prints "sending an email to customer ..." — both only print.
(round 1, re-run) git -C examples/don-hang show stage-0:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Clean/PlaceOrderSplit.cs | wc -l → 38. Also matches quiz q4 context "38 lines of code".

Id check `if (customerId <= 0)` is in FirstProblemWith (line 20) → an upper bound is another check there. TotalWithShippingVnd(List<OrderLine> lines, bool customerIsLoyal) (line 27) already receives customerIsLoyal and decides the 30_000 fee (line 30). Save prints the saving line (34). Notify prints the email line (37). Four methods, one file.

Docs support one class per responsibility: "Attempt to refactor the class by moving some of its responsibilities into new classes." The added "changes only when the steps themselves change" is too strong/ambiguous: Place calls each step with its arguments (lines 8, 11-13), so it also changes when a step's inputs change (e.g. the notifier needing the total, which section 4 itself says it does not need "today").
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: That can stay in `Place`, which would then be all that is left of `PlaceOrderSplit`; its reason to change is the sequence of steps — for example, if the customer had to be told before the order is saved.

claim_verdicts.evidence: (round 1) No SRP passage in refs/dotnet-docs phrases a reason to change by who requests it; heuristic only. Section 3 hedges it ("you can often spot one"); summary line 5 no longer promotes it to the test (round-1 issue resolved).

issues.text: "the steps themselves change" can be read as "when a step's code changes", which contradicts the point that a validator/pricer change stays in its own class; and "only" is too strong, since Place also changes when a step's inputs change (it passes customerId/totalVnd to each step).
issues.quote: it changes only when the steps themselves change, for example if the customer had to be told before the order is saved.
issues.fix: Replace with: "its reason to change is the sequence of steps — for example, if the customer had to be told before the order is saved." Update claim 7 text to match.

issues.text: q5 option c: in this lesson "order" almost always means a customer order, so "The order of check, price, save, notify" made me stop for a second to see it means the sequence of steps.
issues.quote: The order of check, price, save, notify is still decided in one place
issues.fix: Replace "The order of" with "The sequence": "The sequence check, price, save, notify is still decided in one place" (same change in the vi text: "trình tự").
